intro: Muscat rewards visitors with grand mosques, rugged mountains and a lively waterfront corniche. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: No metro or tram; travel is by bus, taxi or car.
Mwasalat buses cover key sights and the airport; fares about 300 baisa to OMR 1.
Pay the bus driver in cash; each bus needs a new ticket.
Orange-and-white taxis are metered-ish; agree the fare first.
OTaxi app gives fixed fares; maxi taxis cost about OMR 0.2-0.4 per hop.
Renting a car is cheap and flexible; a 4WD helps for wadis and mountains.

grand_mosque.name: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque
grand_mosque.hours: Sat–Thu roughly 08:00–11:00 for non-Muslim visitors · closed Friday · check on the day
grand_mosque.tip: Go early morning to see the chandelier and carpet with fewer people. Women cover hair, arms and legs; men wear long trousers.

opera_house.name: Royal Opera House Muscat
opera_house.price_text: Tour tickets vary; performance prices vary by show — check the official programme
opera_house.hours: Box office and building visits vary by season · check on the day
opera_house.tip: Book performances online in advance and arrive early to walk the gardens and arcades.

alam_palace.name: Al Alam Palace
alam_palace.hours: Exterior viewable any time; not open inside
alam_palace.tip: You can only see the gates and facade from the square. Combine it with the forts and Mutrah walk.

muttrah_souq.name: Muttrah Souq
muttrah_souq.price_text: Free to enter · bring cash for shopping
muttrah_souq.hours: Roughly 09:00–13:00 and 16:00–21:00 · longer on weekends · check on the day
muttrah_souq.tip: Haggle politely and start around half the asking price. Best for frankincense, silver and spices.

mutrah_corniche.name: Mutrah Corniche
mutrah_corniche.tip: Walk the full curve at sunset for harbour views and the forts behind you.

forts.name: Al Jalali & Al Mirani Forts
forts.hours: Exterior viewable any time; interiors generally closed to visitors
forts.tip: Photograph them from the Corniche or the palace square. Do not expect to go inside.

shuwa.name: Shuwa
shuwa.price_text: Varies by restaurant — expect a mid-range main course
shuwa.hours: Lunch and dinner at most Omani restaurants
shuwa.tip: Traditional slow-cooked lamb, often served at Eid and festivals. Ask your hotel or a local restaurant where to try it.

fish_market.name: Muttrah Fish Market
fish_market.hours: Busiest early morning · check on the day
fish_market.tip: Arrive before 08:00 to see the catch and the auction buzz.

qurum_beach.name: Qurum Beach
qurum_beach.tip: Good for an evening stroll; the water is calm but check local advice before swimming.

royal_opera_walk.name: Shati Al Qurum walk
royal_opera_walk.tip: A shaded seafront path linking the Opera area to the beach — good for an easy evening walk.

dhow_cruise.name: Muscat harbour dhow cruise
dhow_cruise.price_text: Prices vary by operator — book locally or through your hotel
dhow_cruise.hours: Usually late afternoon and sunset departures
dhow_cruise.tip: A short boat trip from Mutrah shows the forts and palace from the water. Confirm the price and duration before boarding.

ruwi_market.name: Ruwi high street and market area
ruwi_market.hours: Shops roughly 09:00–13:00 and 16:00–21:00 · check on the day
ruwi_market.tip: A busy everyday shopping district, not a tourist souq. Good for cheap eats and local life.

bait_al_zubair.name: Bait Al Zubair museum
bait_al_zubair.price_text: Small entry fee — check on the day
bait_al_zubair.hours: Closed Friday · otherwise daytime hours · check on the day
bait_al_zubair.tip: A compact private museum on Omani life and heritage, close to the palace and souq.

qantab_viewpoint.name: Qantab coastal viewpoint
qantab_viewpoint.tip: A short drive east of Mutrah for rocky coves and clear water. Go early or near sunset.

mutrah_walk.name: Old Mutrah neighbourhood walk
mutrah_walk.hours: Always open · walk in daylight or early evening
mutrah_walk.tip: Wander the lanes behind the souq for old houses and small shops. Dress modestly.

stays.why: Walk to the corniche, fish market and souq. Good for a first visit and evening strolls.
Central and cheap, with bus links. Handy if you are travelling on a budget.
Beaches, cafés and the Royal Opera House nearby. A calm base between old and new Muscat.
Close to the Grand Mosque and the airport road. Good for early flights and mosque visits.

food: Try Omani dishes: shuwa (slow-cooked meat), harees and majboos rice with fish or chicken.
Mutrah fish market: see the catch, then eat grilled fish at simple nearby restaurants.
Omani halwa and dates with cardamom coffee (kahwa) are the classic snack; buy halwa in Mutrah souq.
Cheap eats: shawarma, biryani and cafeteria meals in Ruwi, roughly OMR 1–3 a plate.
Alcohol is limited to licensed hotel restaurants and bars. Dress modestly and ask before photographing people.
more_time: Swap a city day for Nizwa: the fort and Friday goat market, about 1.5–2 hours by car each way.
Add a wadi day: Wadi Shab or Wadi Bani Khalid for pools and walking; check conditions and take a 4WD if unsure.
Take a boat trip from the Marina to watch dolphins, usually a morning outing; book ahead and check the price on the day.
